conditions: Real x tending to zero, with the angle measured in radians.
spoken_aliases: the limit as x approaches zero of sine x divided by x equals one
the limit as x tends to zero of the fraction with numerator sine of x and denominator x equals one

evidence: For 0<x<pi/2 in radians, comparing areas of the inscribed triangle, unit-circle sector and tangent triangle gives sin(x)<x<tan(x). Hence cos(x)<sin(x)/x<1. The squeeze theorem yields the right limit one, and evenness of sin(x)/x gives the same left limit.

Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/3-5-derivatives-of-trigonometric-functions. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
